sentences.text:
2. Heard the arguments of learned counsel for the petitioner.
3.
Learned counsel for the respondent remained absent.

4. The case of the petitioner is that the petitioner is said to be issued a cheque for Rs.45,00,000/-
which came to be dishonoured, hence, the complaint under Section 200 read with Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 (for short 'N.I. Act') filed by the respondent which is under challenge.
5. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that there was a civil dispute between the parties.
An agreement of NC: 2024:KHC:6102 sale entered into between the petitioner and respondent where a legal notice also issued for specific performance of contract.
Subsequently, a complaint under Section 420 of IPC also filed which is pending before the Court where he has filed discharge application which is also pending.
In spite of it, he has filed two cheque cases against this petitioner for issuance of cheque.

Even the legal notice has not been complied under Section 138(c) of the N.I.
Act where no time limit is granted for payment of money.
Therefore, proceeding against the petitioner is abuse of process of law.
Hence, prayed for dismissing the complaint and the proceedings.

6. Having heard the arguments and on perusal of the records, which reveals, there was an agreement of sale entered into between this petitioner with the respondent for selling the property for Rs.95,00,000/-.
He has received Rs.90,00,000/- as advance sale consideration.

Subsequently,
the agreement was not acted upon.
A legal notice was issued by the respondent to this petitioner and in the meanwhile, the respondent also filed a police complaint against this petitioner under Section 420 of IPC.

Subsequently, on behalf of the well wishers and elders, the matter was settled between the parties where the petitioner NC: 2024:KHC:6102 said to be issued two cheques for discharge of sale consideration issued by him for Rs.90,00,000/- under the agreement of sale and the said cheques were dishonoured.
Hence, the complaint came to be filed.

7. On perusal of the records, which clearly reveals, this cheque has been issued by the petitioner for discharging his liability which was received by him as advance sale consideration under the sale agreement.

Of course, the case under Section 420 of IPC also filed for cheating the complainant by this petitioner which is not subject matter before this Court where the petitioner is said to be filed 239 applications for discharge which is pending for consideration.

But the proceedings under Section 138 of N.I. Act initiated by the respondent for having issued the cheque by this petitioner for having dishonour of the cheque which attracts Section 138 of N.I. Act.
If any grievance available in respect of Section 138(c) of N.I. Act for not giving any time for 15 days for payment, that can be considered while conducting the trial on appreciation of evidence.
Such being the case, the question of quashing the criminal proceedings against this petitioner does not arise.
